hero.eyebrow: Whitman College · CCSC Northwestern Regional Hackathon · October 9–10, 2026
hero.title: WhitmHack 2026
hero.subtitle: A 24-hour hackathon bringing together students from across Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and Northern California to tackle real problems proposed by real companies — no theoretical exercises, just build, present, and connect.
taglines: Real companies. Real problems. One weekend.
No CS degree required — bring an idea.

about.title: Built to bridge campus and industry.

bento.heading: Our mission
bento.body: The Pacific Northwest is a growing tech corridor, but structured engagement between companies and student talent is still limited. WhitmHack connects motivated students from across the region with company-proposed challenges — giving companies fresh thinking and giving students a portfolio-ready project and a direct line to industry.
Students expected on campus, in teams of 3–5.

bento.heading: All skill levels welcome
bento.body: WhitmHack is explicitly open to non-CS students. Pre-event learnathons cover tools like Git, APIs, Webflow, and Figma, and roles like researcher, designer, and strategist count just as much as coder.

bento.heading: Hosted at Whitman College
bento.body: WhitmHack runs as part of the CCSC Northwestern Regional Conference at Whitman College this October, organized by the ACM Whitman Chapter with support from the Career and Community Engagement Center (CCEC).

tracks.name: Company Challenge Tracks
tracks.description: Each participating company pitches a real problem they're facing — teams pick a challenge and build a solution over the hackathon.
tracks.prize: Funded from a shared company prize pool (TBD per company)

tracks.name: Visionary Award
tracks.description: For the best-researched solution and prototype, even if the code isn't fully functional — rewards strong thinking over polish.

tracks.name: Humanities Integration Award
tracks.description: For the team that best incorporates ethical, historical, or social perspectives into their technical project.

tracks.name: First-Time Hacker
tracks.description: A dedicated category for hackers at their very first event — eligibility rules TBD.

events.title: Kickoff + Problem Pitches
events.workshopDetails: Company reps present their challenges (~5–7 min each) with a quick Q&A after each. Students mingle and ask clarifying questions.

events.title: Team Formation + Ideation
events.workshopDetails: Participants choose a project, form teams of 3–5, and start brainstorming their approach.

events.title: Dinner Break
events.workshopDetails: Good time for informal networking with sponsors.

events.title: Checkpoint
events.workshopDetails: Updates and progress check-ins with organizers and mentors.

events.title: Build Sprint
events.workshopDetails: Final stretch of building before judging.

events.title: Evaluation
events.workshopDetails: Teams present demos and are judged on innovation, feasibility, technical quality, real-world impact, and clarity of presentation.

questions.question: Who can attend WhitmHack?
questions.answer: Students from colleges and universities across Washington, Oregon, Idaho, and Northern California are welcome — WhitmHack is explicitly designed to be open to non-CS students, not just computer science majors.

questions.question: Do I need coding experience?
questions.answer: No. Pre-event learnathons cover tools like Git, APIs, and AI to help beginners feel comfortable, and roles like researcher/subject-matter-expert, designer, and strategist are just as valued as writing code.

questions.question: Can I use AI tools to build my project?
questions.answer: Yes — AI is allowed as a tool, but participants must be able to explain every line of code. Projects generated entirely from a prompt aren't allowed; teams are encouraged to use AI to reach a higher level of complexity, not to do less work.

questions.question: How much does it cost?
questions.answer: Meals, prizes, and supplies are covered by sponsorship and CS Department support, so there's no cost to participate.

questions.question: What should I bring?
questions.answer: Details TBD — check back closer to the event.
